messages.content:
You map steps of a user scenario in a web application to backend REST requests.
The application: Train Ticket is a microservice-based train ticket booking system for passengers, managing orders, reservations, travel routes, and user accounts.
The backend is a set of Java microservices behind a gateway; a browser UI (ts-ui-dashboard) sends the requests.
Environment: Default Spring profile of every service; gateway on port 18888 routes /api/v1/<service>/** by service name; MySQL 8, RabbitMQ, Nacos; no external network.

Rules:
- Every scenario step sends exactly one HTTP request through the gateway. Pick the one backend handler that serves it, even when the web UI would send several requests or none for that action.
- Some services come in twins: the same API in two services, each keeping its own part of the data. First pick the handler that does what the step asks; then, if that handler has a twin (its card says so), choose the side as the card says, by the data the step works with.
- When a UI variant is sent only under a condition, check the condition against the scenario.
- A request that the web UI sends only in the response handler of another request is the UI's follow-up to that request. A step maps to the first request even when the scenario tells what happens after it; pick the follow-up only when the step asks for the follow-up action by itself.
- Prefer a handler that the web UI calls for this kind of action (candidates show their UI page and action). Handlers without UI are mostly internal APIs that other services call; choose one only when no UI handler does what the step asks.
- Administrator steps (admin console) use admin services; other users' steps do not.
- A step that the system refuses still sends its request: pick the handler that refuses it.

Enum codes used in request fields:
- AssuranceType: TRAFFIC_ACCIDENT=1 (Traffic Accident Assurance, 3.0)
- DocumentType: NONE=0 (Null), ID_CARD=1 (ID Card), PASSPORT=2 (Passport), OTHER=3 (Other)
- Gender: NONE=0 (Null), MALE=1 (Male), FEMALE=2 (Female), OTHER=3 (Other)
- MoneyType: A=Add Money (1), D=Draw Back Money (2)
- OrderStatus: NOTPAID=0 (Not Paid), PAID=1 (Paid & Not Collected), COLLECTED=2 (Collected), CHANGE=3 (Cancel & Rebook), CANCEL=4 (Cancel), REFUNDS=5 (Refunded), USED=6 (Used)
- PaymentType: P=Payment (1), D=Difference (2), O=Outside Payment (3), E=Difference & Outside Payment (4)
- SeatClass: NONE=0 (NoSeat), BUSINESS=1 (GreenSeat), FIRSTCLASS=2 (FirstClassSeat), SECONDCLASS=3 (SecondClassSeat), HARDSEAT=4 (HardSeat), SOFTSEAT=5 (SoftSeat), HARDBED=6 (HardBed), SOFTBED=7 (SoftBed), HIGHSOFTBED=8 (HighSoftSeat)
- Type: G=G (1), D=D (2), Z=Z (3), T=T (4), K=K (5)
- WaitListOrderStatus: NOTPAID=0 (Not Paid), PAID=1 (Paid & Not Collected), COLLECTED=2 (Collected), CANCEL=3 (Cancel), REFUNDS=4 (Refunded), EXPIRED=5 (Expired)

Scenario X9: A new order found only through the refreshed list: price, payment, refund quote and cancellation; then a second booking, payment, collecting the ticket and entering the station
Description: A registered passenger logs in, searches for high-speed (GaoTie/DongChe) trains from Shanghai to Suzhou departing on 1 October 2026, opens the contact book and takes the first contact. They book a first-class seat on the first trip found for this contact, without food, insurance or luggage, and refresh the list of orders, which also holds older orders of the passenger. For the new order they check the price, pay from the internal account balance, ask how much would be refunded and cancel it. Then they book another first-class seat on the same trip for the same contact, refresh the list of orders again, pay for the new order from the internal account balance, collect the ticket and enter the station.
Steps:
1. Log in with username and password
2. Search high-speed (GaoTie/DongChe) trains from Shanghai to Suzhou departing on 1 October 2026
3. Open the contact book and take the first contact
4. Book a first-class seat on the first trip found for this contact, without food, insurance or luggage
5. Refresh the list of orders
6. Check the price of the order
7. Pay for the order from the internal account balance
8. Ask how much would be refunded if the order were cancelled
9. Cancel the order
10. Book another first-class seat on the same trip for the same contact, without food, insurance or luggage
11. Refresh the list of orders
12. Pay for the new order from the internal account balance
13. Collect the ticket for the new order
14. Enter the station with the new order

Requests of earlier steps:
step 1: POST /api/v1/users/login -> UserController#getToken [ts-auth-service] (success)
step 2: POST /api/v1/travelservice/trips/left -> TravelController#queryInfo [ts-travel-service] (success)
step 3: GET /api/v1/contactservice/contacts/account/{accountId} -> ContactsController#findContactsByAccountId [ts-contacts-service] (success)
step 4: POST /api/v1/preserveservice/preserve -> PreserveController#preserve [ts-preserve-service] (success)
step 5: POST /api/v1/orderservice/order/refresh -> OrderController#queryOrdersForRefresh [ts-order-service] (success)
step 6: GET /api/v1/orderservice/order/price/{orderId} -> OrderController#getOrderPrice [ts-order-service] (success)
step 7: POST /api/v1/inside_pay_service/inside_payment -> InsidePaymentController#pay [ts-inside-payment-service] (success)
step 8: GET /api/v1/cancelservice/cancel/refound/{orderId} -> CancelController#calculate [ts-cancel-service] (success)
step 9: GET /api/v1/cancelservice/cancel/{orderId}/{loginId} -> CancelController#cancelTicket [ts-cancel-service] (success)
step 10: POST /api/v1/preserveservice/preserve -> PreserveController#preserve [ts-preserve-service] (success)

Current step 11: Refresh the list of orders
Chosen request: POST /api/v1/orderservice/order/refresh -> OrderController#queryOrdersForRefresh(OrderInfo qi)

Request fields (Java type):
  loginId (body): String
  travelDateStart (body): String
  travelDateEnd (body): String
  boughtDateStart (body): String
  boughtDateEnd (body): String
  state (body): int
  enableTravelDateQuery (body): boolean
  enableBoughtDateQuery (body): boolean
  enableStateQuery (body): boolean
Values the web UI always sends: enableStateQuery=False, enableTravelDateQuery=False, enableBoughtDateQuery=False, travelDateStart=None, travelDateEnd=None, boughtDateStart=None, boughtDateEnd=None

Fill only the fields whose value follows from the step text or the scenario description: the options and extras the step chooses, amounts and quantities, query filters and date ranges, names, numbers and dates of new entities. Do not make up values that the text does not give, such as user names, passwords or codes: they are null. When the step does not take an option ('without ...', 'no ...', or the same choice as an earlier step that did not take it), the fields that the web UI sends only for that option keep their default, and coded fields get the enum code for none. Fields that an edit does not change are null. Use enum codes from the reference for coded fields. Use null for identifiers, for values known only from results of earlier steps, and for everything the text does not determine. Places and dates are not identifiers: when the request acts on a record that an earlier step searched for or opened by places and a date the text names, fill those places and that date from the text.
